title: How car engines work
examples: How does the piston move up and down?
What is the difference between the intake and exhaust strokes?
Does the crankshaft make the engine run?

explain.say: Today we will learn how a car engine works. It uses a special four-stroke cycle. This cycle helps make the car move forward.

items: Power: Controlled explosion pushes the piston
Exhaust: Used gases leave the cylinder

draw.text: Four-Stroke Cycle: Intake, Compression, Power, Exhaust

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a piston engine. Look at the spark plug, the intake valve and the exhaust valve. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
First is the intake stroke. The piston moves down, sucking in a fuel and air mixture. This prepares the cylinder for the next step.
Next is compression. The piston moves up, squeezing the mixture into a small space. This squeeze builds up a lot of pressure inside.
The power stroke happens next. A spark ignites the compressed mixture, causing a strong explosion. This explosion forces the piston down with great force.
Finally, the exhaust stroke. The piston moves up again, pushing all the burnt gases out. These used gases must leave the engine completely.

The piston moves up and down inside the cylinder. This straight up and down motion is connected to the crankshaft. The crankshaft turns this straight motion into circular motion. This spinning motion turns the wheels.

faq.q: What is the purpose of the spark plug?
faq.a: The spark plug creates the initial spark needed for combustion. Without it, the fuel and air mixture will not ignite properly. You might also ask what starts the explosion, or what ignites the mixture.
asks: How does the engine get started?
What causes the burn in the cylinder?

faq.q: Does the engine run on gasoline or diesel?
faq.a: Most common car engines use gasoline, which requires a spark plug. Diesel engines work differently and do not need a spark plug. You could also ask what fuel the engine uses, or how the ignition works.
asks: What kind of fuel is needed?
Is a spark plug always used?

faq.q: What is the role of the valves in the engine?
faq.a: The valves control the flow of gases into and out of the cylinder. They open for intake or exhaust, and close tightly when needed. Students might ask how the gases get in and out, or what controls the openings.
asks: How do the gases move in and out?

faq.q: Why is the power stroke the most important one?
faq.a: The power stroke is important because it creates the force that moves the car. This force is what turns the crankshaft and makes the wheels spin. Other ways to ask this are what makes the car go, or where the energy comes from.
asks: Which stroke actually pushes the car?
Where does the turning force come from?

faq.q: If the piston stops moving, what happens to the car?
faq.a: If the piston stops moving, the engine stops, and the car will slow down and stop. The engine needs continuous combustion to keep turning the crankshaft. You could ask what happens if the engine stalls, or what keeps the motion going.
asks: Does the crankshaft need the piston?

facts: The four-stroke cycle includes intake, compression, power, and exhaust.
In the intake stroke, the piston moves down, drawing in the air and fuel mixture.
The crankshaft converts the linear up and down motion into rotational motion.
The power stroke is caused by the rapid expansion of hot gases.

quiz.say: Which stroke is responsible for the actual force that moves the car?
quiz.why: The power stroke is when the explosion pushes the piston, creating the force.

wrong.0: This stroke only pushes the used gases out.
wrong.2: This stroke only brings the fuel and air mixture in.
wrong.3: This stroke only squeezes the mixture, it does not push.

quiz.say: What component changes straight up and down movement into spinning movement?
quiz.why: The crankshaft is specifically designed to convert linear motion into rotary motion.

wrong.0: The cylinder head covers the top and does not convert motion.
wrong.2: The piston only moves up and down inside the cylinder.
wrong.3: The spark plug only provides the electrical spark.

quiz.say: If the engine is running, which process must have just finished to allow the next step to start?
quiz.why: The engine must push out all the used gases during the exhaust stroke before fresh air can enter.

wrong.1: The intake stroke happens after the exhaust gases have left.
wrong.2: Compression happens after the mixture has been drawn in.
wrong.3: The power stroke happens after the mixture has been compressed.
